about.title: Palo Alto Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Palo Alto blends dense retail corridors along University Avenue, tech campuses, and older residential streets, which means the conditions behind a fall vary widely — a cracked walkway near Middlefield Road, a slick floor inside a café, a poorly lit apartment stairwell. Whatever the setting, California law asks a specific question: did the property owner know, or should they have reasonably known, about the hazard, and did they fail to fix or warn about it? That single issue often decides a premises liability claim. Because evidence like spill logs, maintenance records, and surveillance footage can disappear quickly, documenting the scene and reporting the fall matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured people in Palo Alto with an independent attorney who can evaluate the hazard, gather evidence before it's gone, and explain your options. There's no cost to get connected, and no fee owed unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why the Details Matter in a Premises Case

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Evidence
items.desc: California requires showing the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can pull maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to build that case.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many stores and buildings overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that footage can be critical to your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: Even if you were partly distracted or moving quickly when you fell, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows you to recover a share of damages reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Palo Alto?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit in California. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city building or park, the deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claims process. Talking to an attorney early helps make sure you don't miss a critical window.

items.question: What if I fell at a business near University Avenue or a downtown Palo Alto shop?
items.answer: Commercial property owners and tenants are expected to keep walkways, floors, and entrances reasonably safe for customers. If a hazard existed long enough that staff should have noticed and addressed it, that supports a notice argument. An attorney can help identify who's responsible — the store, the landlord, or a maintenance contractor.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in our network generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
